cards.title: Transaction and publication
items: DECLARED: the admin operation first checks Shipment ownership/existence through internal HTTP, then atomically commits tracking + outbox.
EventId is the stable logical identity; EventBridge and SQS transport IDs are not deduplication keys.
Publication and downstream processing are independent. A crash after PutEvents success but before marking published can deliver duplicates.

cards.title: Commit before ACK
items: Duplicate EventId: durable inbox prevents a second effect. Delayed/stale sequence is classified without regressing state.
Missing predecessor: retry without advancing the checkpoint. Invalid transitions have a durable rejected outcome.
Only a durable acknowledged outcome permits DeleteMessage; a transient failure remains retryable.

cards.title: Three distinct failure stores
items: EventBridge delivery DLQ: target-delivery retries exhausted (10 retries / one hour).
Consumer DLQ: source queue redrive after maxReceiveCount 5. It does not repair ordering.
Outbox quarantine: exhausted publication attempts remain in PostgreSQL for explicit operator disposition.

cards.title: What was demonstrated
items: PROVEN on 29 October: two event sequences reached persisted Shipment effects through EventBridge/SQS.
HISTORICAL: the broader 24 October retry, deduplication and failure tests were not all repeated.
At-least-once transport, idempotent effects; no exactly-once delivery claim.
